# My Interview Problems

This chapter stores ideas, core concepts, and programming examples for interview questions that I like to ask candidates. These questions are designed to evaluate a candidate's problem-solving skills, coding proficiency, and ability to handle progressive constraints.

### Interview Problem Format {#intro-interview-format}

Each problem in this chapter is structured to facilitate a technical interview:

- **Problem Statement**: A clear and concise description of the task presented to the candidate.
- **Examples**: Sample inputs and expected outputs to clarify the requirements and edge cases.
- **Core Idea**: The main algorithmic concept or data structure the candidate is expected to identify.
- **Walkthrough & Implementation**: A step-by-step explanation and a reference implementation (typically in Java).
- **Follow-up Questions**: A series of progressive challenges, rated by difficulty (e.g., Easy, Medium, Hard), to test the candidate's depth of understanding and ability to optimize their solution under new constraints.

### Problem Overview {#intro-problem-overview}

Here is a summary of the interview problems designed in this collection, targeting different experience levels and focus areas.

| Problem Name | Core Difficulty | Follow-up Range | Ideal Candidate (YoE) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Role-Based Feature Evaluator](#interview-feature-evaluator) | Easy | Easy - Medium | Junior to Mid (0-3 yrs) |
| [The Polluted State Test Finder](#interview-polluted-state-test-finder) | Medium | Easy - Hard | Mid to Senior (3-8 yrs) |
| [AST Linter & The Visitor Pattern](#interview-ast-linter) | Medium/Hard | Medium - Hard | Mid to Senior (4-8+ yrs) |
| [The Microservice Deadlock](#interview-microservice-deadlock) | Hard | Medium - Hard | Senior to Staff (5-10+ yrs) |
